props.title: Images

sections.content: Robert Altman's psychological horror masterpiece Images represents one of the most unsettling explorations of mental breakdown ever filmed. Susannah York delivers a haunting performance as Cathryn, a children's author whose grip on reality splinters at a remote Irish country house. The film shares DNA with Roman Polanski's Repulsion (1965) and Rosemary's Baby (1968) in its claustrophobic portrayal of female psychological disintegration, but Altman's experimental approach - with its overlapping soundscapes and reality-bending imagery - pushes even further into pure subjective madness.

sections.content: The film's revolutionary sound design by Stomu Yamash'ta creates an otherworldly atmosphere where reality and hallucination become indistinguishable. This influenced later psychological horror films like Possession (1981) and David Lynch's Lost Highway (1997). Vilmos Zsigmond's cinematography employs unsettling compositions and mirror imagery that would later be echoed in Stanley Kubrick's The Shining (1980), particularly in its use of doubles and doppelgangers.

York's performance, which won her Best Actress at Cannes, captures the terrifying dissolution of self that would later be explored in films like Mulholland Drive (2001) and Black Swan (2010). The film's rural Irish setting becomes a character itself, with the isolation and misty landscape contributing to the psychological claustrophobia in ways that influenced later works like Lars von Trier's Antichrist (2009). sections.content: The legacy of Images can be seen in contemporary psychological horror films that blur the line between reality and madness. Films like The Babadook (2014) and Saint Maud (2020) draw from Altman's pioneering work in subjective horror, while Alex Garland's Men (2022) directly references the film's use of doppelgangers and rural isolation. The way Images handles its unreliable narrator and questioning of reality laid groundwork for mind-bending contemporary works like Upstream Color (2013) and The Lighthouse (2019).
